sections.heading: Glamsterdam Application Readiness Update
sections.summary: All 3 high-severity affected projects will fix by mid-December; medium-severity projects will be ready by January 10 at the latest.
sections.body:
- Rahul reported that the EF, ChainSecurity, and Dedaub have collectively reached out to at least 50 companies with confirmed impact from Glamsterdam's gas repricing.
- Of the 3 high-severity affected projects, all have either already fixed or will fix by mid-December.
- Medium-severity projects have confirmed readiness ranging from next week to January 10.
- Mid-January was presented as the earliest reasonable mainnet date, assuming no spec changes.
- ChainSecurity's public impact assessment report was shared: https://www.chainsecurity.com/security-audit/eip-8037-eip-8038-impact-assessment/
- Spencer noted EIP-8037 affected around 11% of broken contracts; the rest are gas-repricing-related.
- Lido representatives requested end of January at minimum for mainnet, citing governance vote timelines (10-day vote period, plus holidays).

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Spec Change Debate
sections.summary: No concrete spec change proposals emerged; most client teams favored keeping the current spec, with Hoodi go/no-go deferred to next week's ACDC.
sections.body:
- Besu argued that breaking try/catch behavior in Solidity is qualitatively different from breaking hard-coded gas assumptions, and warranted exploring spec fixes.
  - The concern is that contracts relying on gas accounting invariants (e.g., gas remaining after sub-calls) are broken in ways developers cannot easily anticipate or fix.
- Nethermind had proposed spec changes 3+ weeks ago but acknowledged uncertainty about whether full due diligence on alternative breakage had been done.
- Reth/Dragan argued that any form of two-dimensional gas will inevitably break some contracts; EIP-8037 is good enough and should ship as-is.
  - Recommended creating developer guidelines and approved patterns for future gas-related changes.
- Geth/Marius explained the most popular candidate change — moving refunds to end of transaction — would break contracts relying on mid-execution refund behavior (e.g., write-then-clear patterns), potentially reducing effective state writes per transaction.
- Toni Wahrstaetter noted 90-95% of affected contracts are broken by pure repricing, not by something a spec change could address.
- Multiple participants warned that any spec change would restart the full fork shipping process (new audits, devnets, testnets, outreach) adding months of delay and potentially introducing new breakage.
  - Francesco D'Amato pointed out spec changes could break additional contracts that currently work because they benefit from refund mechanics.
- Solidity team (Radek) offered to prepare a deeper analysis on the try/catch OOG problem for the following week.
- CL-side concern flagged by Justin Traglia and Ben Edgington: a potential consensus-breaking change regarding payload binding on the CL side is still unresolved.
  - Spec proposal: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5820
  - Potuz noted this change is "not small."
- Client team positions polled:
  - Geth: pencil in Hoodi, don't push timelines further.
  - Besu: would prefer spec change, but accepts if no one else does; no reason not to schedule if spec is unchanged.
  - Nethermind: fine scheduling; would appreciate further analysis but not blocking.
  - Reth: schedule it, ship current spec.
  - ethrex: schedule now, no spec changes.
  - Erigon: preferred investing effort in spec changes to preserve smart contract immutability; concerned about rushing.
- Decision: pencil in Hoodi fork for the week of December 14 (likely Dec 16-17); final go/no-go decision deferred to next ACDC call in one week.
  - EL devs encouraged to attend ACDC to participate in the decision.
  - Anyone advocating for spec changes has one week to present a specific, well-analyzed candidate change.
- Next ACDT on Monday will also discuss lessons learned from Glamsterdam's process to improve future forks.

sections.heading: Hegota Fork Scope Options
sections.summary: Most teams favored freezing near current devnet scope (frames bundle + PQ additions); final scoping decisions deferred to ACDE in two weeks.
sections.body:
- Ansgar presented 5 levels of scope restriction for Hegota, from most to least aggressive:
  1. Enshrined PQ only (drop frames entirely) — no support voiced.
  2. Core frames EIP only, nothing else.
  3. Core frames bundle (frames + recent roots + keyed nonces + tx assertions).
  4. Smaller scope (under 10 EIPs total, disciplined selection).
  5. Normal scope (10-15 EIPs, business as usual).
- Currently ~19 CFI/SFI EIPs on the EL side for Hegota.
- Client team positions:
  - Nethermind: all EIPs already implemented at some level; prefer not reducing scope but willing to cut off if CL is ready sooner; between options 4 and 5.
  - ethrex: between options 3 and 4; freeze current scope, leave window open for 8288-compatible PQ signature enshrinement; testing is the bottleneck, not implementation.
  - Besu: bogota-devnet-2 is a reasonable freezing point; prioritize SPHINCS and signature aggregation next; effectively option 2-3 plus PQ additions.
  - Nethermind/Ben Adams: if reducing scope doesn't actually accelerate the fork (because PQ decisions aren't ready), there's no point in reducing scope.
- Toni Wahrstaetter cautioned against shipping frames without companion EIPs (recent roots, keyed nonces, tx assertions), as changing the transaction object later would hurt app-layer adoption.
- Greg Colvin spoke against removing EIPs from forks, noting personal and community impact of repeated delays and broken commitments.
- Ben Adams requested that remaining PFI EIPs be explicitly processed (CFI or DFI) rather than silently dropped.
  - Only 3 PFI items remain: 8368, 8372, 7907.
- Kevaundray Wedderburn flagged that EIP-8151 (ecRecover changes) could break many contracts, requiring similar outreach as EIP-8037.
  - Preliminary chain analysis shared: https://github.com/kevaundray/pq-chain-analysis/tree/main
- Action item: all client teams to prepare a short written position (1-2 paragraphs) on preferred Hegota scope by end of next week, for discussion at ACDE in two weeks.
- Priority ordering from pre-Devcon referenced: https://forkcast.org/upgrade/hegota/priority-order/

sections.heading: PQ Signature Scheme Discussion (leanSPHINCS vs ML-DSA)
sections.summary: Hash-based leanSPHINCS remains the primary enshrined scheme; Matt (Geth) argued for also supporting ML-DSA given its industry adoption.
sections.body:
- Mislav (Ethlabs) reported from wallet conversations that there is appetite for ML-DSA and other signing schemes, and some wallets don't feel urgent PQ pressure.
  - Wallets want frames to be scheme-agnostic with multiple canonical verifier contracts.
  - Key management for smooth PQ transition (e.g., EIP-8130 or similar) identified as important for wallet adoption.
- Nico explained that ML-DSA EVM verifiers have been optimized to ~800K gas (with Keccak) or ~1.6M gas (with NIST SHAKE), and Falcon to ~500K gas.
  - Verifier contracts: https://github.com/ZKNoxHQ/ETHDILITHIUM and https://github.com/ZKNoxHQ/ETHFALCON
  - ML-DSA precompile was DFI'd; decision was based on hash-based cryptography being the most conservative option.
- Matt (Geth) argued that leanSPHINCS is non-standard and will lack industry support compared to NIST-standardized ML-DSA, drawing parallels to the K1 curve adoption problems.
  - Advocated giving users multiple PQ options to maximize migration likelihood.
- Potuz supported enshrining one PQ signature scheme in Hegota so the community (especially rollups) can begin upgrading immediately.
  - SPHINCS adds no new crypto assumptions beyond what Ethereum already uses (Keccak).
- Antonio Sanso urged focusing on hash-based cryptography, hinting that reasons would become clearer in coming weeks.
- Dragan agreed leanSPHINCS is the right near-term choice; expects better schemes from NIST standardization in a few years.
- Mislav emphasized this is a product/UX decision, not purely cryptographic — wallets need signing schemes their hardware (iPhone, etc.) can natively use.
- Discussion deferred to a future dedicated call; Ansgar noted today's focus should remain on fork scoping.

sections.heading: Frame Transactions Breakout Summary and leanSPHINCS Proposal
sections.summary: Frames spec targeting completion by mid-December; ethrex proposed a minimal 8288-compatible leanSPHINCS EIP for Hegota.
sections.body:
- Matt summarized the frames breakout:
  - Working on 8288 forward compatibility — considering changes to or removal of the signature list in favor of frame mode mechanism.
  - Investigating tree-root-style hashing for the transaction format (Etan to write PR in coming weeks).
  - Goal: frames spec essentially complete by mid-December (before holidays), with only small implementation-driven changes afterward.
- Iván (ethrex) presented a draft proposal for minimal leanSPHINCS native signatures on top of frames, designed to be 8288-compatible without requiring aggregation or proofs initially.
  - EIP PR: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12672
  - Specs still being written; will be proposed for Hegota at next ACDE.
- Nico reported that the frames breakout found a way to do PQ multisig: one owner sends a frame transaction from their PQ account, Safe checks other owners inside execTransaction through EIP-1271.
  - No changes required to Safe or EIP-8141.
  - Documentation: https://github.com/nconsigny/SPHINCS-/blob/main/docs/safe-pq-owners.md

sections.heading: Hegota Devnet Next Steps
sections.summary: No cross-layer devnet until CL decisions on FOCIL are finalized; EL devnets to pause at current scope with possible additions decided on ACDT Monday.
sections.body:
- Agreement: no cross-layer (CL+EL) devnet for now; wait for CL-side decisions on FOCIL scope.
- For EL-only devnets, discussion split between pausing at current scope (to harden frames testing) versus adding a few more EIPs.
- Barnabas proposed Bogota devnet 3 scoping with cleanup EIPs (e.g., removing bloom filters, removing storage clear refund) and updated frames spec, without FOCIL.
- Mario (testing team) noted significant frames testing remains, including mempool testing; hardening time would be well-used but not opposed to adding more EIPs if client devs agree.
- Potuz noted CL pre-registration (without full PQ) could be done in one week; suggested it could ship with a minimal CL fork alongside EL Hegota.
  - Pre-reg doesn't require a hard fork per se; consuming pre-registrations does.
- Ben Adams argued for still adding small, isolated cleanup EIPs (e.g., removing bloom filters) that are unaffected by PQ decisions, rather than stalling all progress.
- Decision: default to pausing at current devnet scope; ACDT on Monday can revisit and approve new devnet additions if there is appetite.
  - Barnabas and others can propose specific cleanup EIPs for consideration.
- Separate CL and EL devnets to be maintained until FOCIL and CL PQ decisions are made.
- Ben Edgington gave a rough estimate of mid-2028 for a realistic CL PQ ship date ("don't quote me"); Potuz suggested targeting EOY 2027 to actually ship mid-2028.
- Ansgar reminded all EL devs to attend the next two ACDC calls (in 1 week and 3 weeks) for FOCIL and cross-layer coordination decisions.
